Jared —

Appreciate the clarity. I’ve attached a fresh worksheet (commit_pricing_model.xlsx) and a short sensitivity chart (gpu_sensitivity_chart.png) that map out three commit tenors (12/24/36 months) and how per-token/unit economics move with +/- 20% GPU cost swings. High level summary:

- 12 months: lowest up-front discount (approx 18%) but most flexible; unit price is most exposed to GPU cost swings (delta ~+/-14% for +/-20% GPU cost).
- 24 months: mid discount (~26%); you get improved protection (delta ~+/-9%).
- 36 months: best effective discount (~33%) and the smallest delta (~+/-6%), but requires stronger termination language.

We can offer a price collar for 24-months: auto-adjust up to a 10% pass-through if GPU index moves beyond our agreed threshold, with a bilateral cap of 15% annualized. To avoid legal churn we propose:

1) An agreed GPU index (public cloud GPU spot index + vendor list)
2) A three-tier collar: +/-10% buffer with 0 pass-through, beyond that a 50/50 split up to the 15% cap.
3) Quarterly review cadence; either party can trigger a reprice review with 30 days notice.

Irene — can you confirm GovCloud constraints (RPO/RTO/SLA differences, hosting surcharge) and whether the collar/escrow approach needs security sign-off? Marcus — please confirm the margin delta and whether we need exec sign-off for a 15% cap. Karthik — can you run a quick scenario for how this offer affects committed capacity sizing in Q4 plan?

If you’re open to it Jared, we can lock the 24-month with the collar in a term sheet and route the 15% cap through an approval by EPD/Finance. That would keep legal focused on SOW/controls rather than reworking pricing mechanics.

Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Headline: we can accommodate the proposed 24-month collar with the 50/50 split and a 15% cap, but it requires a one-time approval for an incremental discount of ~3.5% off list to preserve target margin at the midpoint scenario. If leadership signs off on that incremental concession, Ops is comfortable sizing the dedicated pool as follows:

- Burst/overcommit buffer: additional 12 GPUs in a shared pool for 20% peak tolerance.
- Re-eval: cadence aligned to quarters; automatic re-provisioning trigger if actual utilization >80% for two consecutive quarters.

Approval path suggested: Finance + CRO sign-off for the 3.5% concession, Legal to accept collar language, and Infra to publish index formula. Sean — I’ll prepare the short approval package (pricing delta, capacity plan, P&L sensitivity) and ping CRO for exec sign-off today.
